text:
maria_support: Customer reported a sudden spike in latency and cross-region requests for their EU tenant, billing also shows requests routed to us-west-1 :frowning:
customer_jess: seeing 600-900ms p50 to our EU app since 03:15 UTC, used to be ~60ms. all requests come from our app server behind a vendor proxy.
maria_support: I pulled a sample request from their logs, looks like we got an extra header from the proxy: `X-Client-Region: ` (empty string).
maria_support: repro curl from their env: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Client-Region:" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> router picked us-west (closest edge to proxy), not eu-west.
ingrid_sre: :eyes: do we treat empty header as explicit region preference or ignore?
jason_edge: Router decision tree: check query param -> header -> auth claims -> default/geo. Implementation currently treats a header present (even empty) as higher precedence; empty value winds up parsed to "" and code falls back to default edge selection algorithm (closest POP = us-west).
maria_support: Customer expectation was header absent so auth claim (eu tenant) would win. They pinned model/tenant to eu region so billing shows cross-region costs.
proxy-bot: automated-note: proxy-v2.4.1 was deployed to the vendor last week; change log mentions "preserve header keys, even when values empty" for debugging.
customer_jess: vendor confirmed they started forwarding an empty X-Client-Region for debugging, did not expect it to change routing.
ingrid_sre: short-term mitigation: instruct router to treat empty or whitespace-only region header as absent. I'll open a canary rule to strip empty headers at the edge.
jason_edge: can we get a reproducer? I can run a curl from edge-lab with an empty header and grab router trace.
maria_support: repro steps for SRE: 1) `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Region:" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` 2) check `router.trace` header in response and our ingress logs 3) compare with `-H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1"`
jason_edge: trace snippet from lab run: `router.decision=[header_present]; header.value=""; selected_route=closest_pop(us-west-1); fallback_policy=none`
ingrid_sre: Proposed fix: modify Router.isRegionHeaderValid() to `trim(value).length > 0` and fall through as if header missing when false. Also add quick patch to edge-nginx config to drop header when empty for canary.
maria_support: Customer asked for ETA and refund escalation: opened internal ticket INC-2023 with billing flagged. asked for temporary routing override to force eu for that API key.
jason_edge: I can add a per-key override in the routing table, ETA 2-4 hours for canary change. Will push strip-empty-header rule to canary after tests.
ingrid_sre: Risk: some customers may intentionally send empty header for probing; behavior change is low risk since semantics should be "absent". We'll run canary in eu region first.
maria_support: Customer accepts temporary override + will revert vendor change. They asked to be notified when permanent fix is out.
proxy-bot: note: created ticket RUNTIME-579 to track code fix; linked to INC-2023.
jason_edge: pushed edge-nginx drop-empty-header config to canary (eu-pop-1). Observability: new canary now shows requests with `X-Client-Region:` are treated as absent and route to eu as expected.
maria_support: confirmed with customer — their next 50 requests now land in eu and latency returned to ~70ms. Customer requested formal postmortem and a note in docs about header handling.
ingrid_sre: followups: 1) PR to router runtime to validate region header (RUNTIME-579), 2) add an item in API docs: "Empty X-Client-Region headers are ignored" 3) add a regression test for multi-value/empty values.
maria_support: filing docs/eng-actions and notifying billing for refund calculation. closing this thread when RUNTIME-579 merged and docs published. :white_check_mark:
